title: The band's trip north to the Harlem Opera House
summary: The school bus took the band on one-nighters to Asbury Park; Frank Schiffman heard them and booked the Harlem Opera House in 1934.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: How did the band get to New York?

Oh, the school bus. We went up during a tour of one-night stands up to Asbury Park. And, from Asbury Park, we went into Elizabeth, New Jersey. That was supposed to be the last date, and then turn around and go back to the school.

Frank Schiffman of the Apollo heard about the band over there. He came over to listen to us. So, he liked us, and he booked us into the Harlem Opera House. And, that's how we happened to get into New York. We went into the Harlem Opera House.
And then, we had turn away crowds at that time. Then, we went out and did Philadelphia, Baltimore, (inaudible), and Washington. And then, back to the Harlem Opera House, you know, and the big crowds.
And then, I happened to be back stage and one of the fellows from the Ubanqi Club came up to talk to me about going in there.
And the boys, after we finished, were still going back to school. They said, 'We'll stick with you if you can still keep us going. We'll stick with you.'
And you, you started in school, and you had a tour coming up to Asbury Park. Where did you stop in between?
Well, the different, I don't understand, but we was playing different cities in different states, you know, all the way up, doing one night stands like the last one.
Sort of all the way up from Birmingham.
From Birmingham all the way up to Asbury Park.
Like these one night stands. We was doing the same thing.
